summary.headline: IFB Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.65% to INR 1,529 crore, with PAT up to INR 38.06 crore, but commodity and forex costs were not passed on.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.65% YoY to INR 1,529 crore and PBDIT rose 26.46% to INR 88.46 crore, with margin at 5.79% of revenue versus 5.34%. PAT was INR 38.06 crore (2.5% of revenue) against INR 25.36 crore a year earlier. Management said commodity and forex headwinds are not behind the company and that it has not been able to pass them on in price, relying instead on cost initiatives (INR 42-43 crore in Q1). Home Appliances (HAD) revenue grew about 18%, with July described as good, while gross margin fell about 160 bps.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 vs Q1 FY26; FY26 HAD growth was about 9.8-10%
FY26 full year: about INR 67 crore
Attributed to raw material price increase of about INR 4,125 per tonne in the quarter

segments.name: Home Appliances (HAD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 18% in Q1; front-load volume up 9-10%, top-load volume up over 20%, AC volume up 6-8%, and IFB-branch refrigerator volume up 14% per management. Gross margin down about 160 bps on material costs.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Sales up 17% YoY and above budget; EBITDA in line with budget. Management expects similar growth going forward, with festive season supportive. Stated FY ambition of about INR 2,000 crore revenue; current base about INR 1,000-1,100 crore.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Loss-making in Q1 due to steel price increases, which management expects to recover from customers in coming quarters. Management cited ROCE of about 20%.

segments.name: Services (HAD)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 17% in the quarter per management. Profitability described as double-digit at PBT level; management did not give a figure.

segments.name: IFB Refrigeration (associate, 41.40% stake)
segments.commentary: Company PBT INR 80 lakh; IFB share INR 0.33 crore (INR 33 lakh) in Q1 versus a loss last year. Company revenue growth stated at 2%. Management declined to discuss it in detail.

guidance_outlook: Management expects about 20% growth, with Q1 at 18% and July described as good; it said it is 'working towards' 20%.
Cost initiatives target of INR 120-150 crore for FY27, with INR 42-43 crore already in Q1; the company said it is not cutting counters or in-store promoters.
Management has no near-term view that commodity and forex pressure is over and did not expect to pass it fully through.
PBDIT should be early double digit in the long term, per the CEO (in response to an analyst question on margin aspiration).
Engineering expects growth similar to Q1. The INR 2,000 crore target depends partly on a battery project (LOI about INR 150 crore from Tata) that is now under review after Tata Sons' decision.
Full-year capex is about INR 110 crore; the Engineering stamping capex plan is about INR 400 crore.
AC aspiration: 7-10% market share, with no timeline given.
capex_capacity: AC capacity about 75,000 units per month; peak month utilisation about 85%. Debottlenecking and automation planned to reach 75,000-80,000 per month without adding shifts.
Management said there is no current capacity constraint in HAD and that new products for unserved capacities are expected within 3-6 months.

Engineering acquired land in Gujarat for EV and stamping. Stamping capacity expansion planned in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore, with a business target of about INR 1,000 crore against about INR 400 crore stamping capex.
Tata LOI (about INR 150 crore) for battery project under review; land already acquired, and machinery not yet ordered.
demand_pricing: Price increases taken across all HAD categories in the last quarter, but not enough to cover commodity and forex; management said it had led some price increases where the market had not.
Management said it has not been able to pass commodity and forex cost increases to customers in full; pricing is constrained by competitiveness.
Front-load washer share estimated to be top-2 by management, but no published market-share data is available. Top-load may be lower.
Trade schemes and discounts of about INR 1,800 crore were questioned by an analyst; management said it is an industry practice and under review for leakages.
RAC transition: old-rating AC stock was run down by about January, and the company did not build older-rated stock. Management said the new-rated models are 10-15% more expensive than the market.

qa_highlights.question: Has the commodity and forex headwind (about INR 170 crore across Q4 and Q1) been passed on, and is it behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Not behind us. Management said it has not passed commodity or forex costs to customers; savings came from efficiency initiatives instead.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RAC growth (about 10%) lag the industry (20%+)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company chose not to carry older-rated AC stock through the BEE rating change, so it lost the price advantage. It is focusing on higher-capacity models.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company sustaining 20% growth and what drove the Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 HAD revenue grew 18%, and management said distribution fixes (counters, displays, promoters) drove growth; it says the trend should continue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 2,000 crore Engineering target still achievable given the battery project uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 250 crore of business is near closing, and that the existing business grows about 20%. The battery project is under review, and other projects are being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Was the company's cost-savings guidance lowered from INR 150-200 crore to INR 120-150 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is INR 120-150 crore for FY27, after INR 67 crore in FY26; SKU rationalisation is expected to add benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Why did IFB refrigeration company growth (2%) differ from IFB-branch refrigerator sales growth (14%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 14% is IFB Industries branch volume and that the company's own figure could differ because of branch structure; it declined to discuss the associate.

risks_watch: Commodity (steel, copper and others) and forex pressure with no pass-through; gross margin down about 160 bps.
Steel division loss in Q1 with recovery depending on customer price pass-through in coming quarters.
Engineering growth target depends on OEM business wins and the Tata battery project, which is under review.
Trade-scheme spend of about INR 1,800 crore (per an analyst) and its scrutiny by management.
Motor division loss; management deferred the question to an offline discussion, so the cause is unclear.
Inconsistent Fine Blanking Q1 FY26 revenue figure (INR 185-186 crore vs INR 176 crore) in the presentation; management said it would revert.
key_quotes: Commodity and Forex continues to be an issue. So even when you look at Q1, we have an issue as far as commodity and Forex is concerned.
No, we have not been able to pass on commodity and Forex to the market.
So the 20%, as I said, that is definitely what we are working towards. And Q1 has been at 18% growth, as far as revenue is concerned.
So PBDIT should be early double digit in my opinion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and distribution execution (18% HAD growth, July described as good), but cautious and evasive on commodity and forex, pricing pass-through, and the Tata battery project, which management said is under review. Management declined to discuss IFB Refrigeration (the associate) in detail and deferred the Motor division and Fine Blanking base questions offline.
